q: Is there a concretely constructible 'modified' non-abelian QHS algorithm on S_N whose Fourier statistic sees conjugacy-class information (not just normal-subgroup information) and thereby distinguishes Stab_{j_0} from Stab_{j_1}? The paper leaves this as its central open question. Our Part-D verification pins the failure mode down: it is entirely explained by (i) Hallgren-Russell-Ta-Shma's normal-subgroup restriction and (ii) mutual conjugacy of the Stab_j -- any hypothetical modification must break at least one of these, e.g. by conditioning on a coset representative rather than on a Fourier label alone.
basis: In Part D we directly enumerated the largest normal subgroup of S_N contained in Stab_0 for N=3,4,5 and confirmed it is {e}. In Part E we noted Ind_{Stab_0}^{S_N}(1) = trivial + standard, which is dwarfed by the regular representation Ind_{{e}}^{S_N}(1). This gives a concrete finite handle on 'what statistical information the standard QHS is throwing away.'
next_steps: Implement a coset-state-based sampler (not just character-based) that measures in a basis mixing different irreducible components; test on S_4 whether such a sampler achieves \Omega(1) success on Grover's HSP at N=4, and compare its query count to the O(\sqrt N)=2 Grover-optimum. Publish the negative or positive result. Zalka's bound puts a hard ceiling at O(\sqrt N).

q: How does the Grover-state invariance under Stab_{j_0} degrade under realistic noise? Our Part-B fidelity is exactly 1 in a noise-free statevector; but under depolarising or amplitude-damping channels the invariance should decay at a rate that is a diagnostic for how much 'hidden symmetry' the physical device still respects.
basis: We ran only noiseless Statevector simulation. The paper is theoretical and gives no noise model. But the invariance is a symmetry statement, and symmetry-preservation vs symmetry-breaking under noise is exactly the kind of thing that shows up on real hardware benchmarks (cf. mirror-benchmarking, cycle-benchmarking).
next_steps: Repeat Part B on Qiskit's density-matrix simulator with per-gate depolarising noise p in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}; plot mean Stab-fidelity vs p and fit the decay. Then run on ibm_kyoto or a small trapped-ion device for N=4 and compare.

q: What is the smallest finite group G with subgroup H such that: (a) H is non-normal, (b) the largest normal subgroup of G in H is {e}, (c) the Stab-analog subgroups are pairwise conjugate, AND YET some published non-abelian QHS algorithm still identifies H? A concrete positive example would rule out the strongest possible generalisation of the paper's negative result.
basis: The paper's Section-9 obstruction is exactly (a)+(b)+(c). If any group at all admits an efficient QHS despite (a)+(b)+(c), that carves out precisely the 'modified QHS' the paper asks about.
next_steps: Survey the literature (Ivanyos-Magniez-Santha, Moore-Rockmore-Russell-Sniady, Kuperberg dihedral) for known efficient non-abelian QHS instances and check condition (b) for each. Any counter-example would be immediately publishable.

q: Does the paper's 'HSP = Grover' reformulation extend cleanly to Grover with M > 1 marked elements (M-marked amplitude amplification)? The stabiliser subgroup then becomes Stab_{j_1,...,j_M} = intersection of individual stabilisers, which is generally smaller. Does Section 7 still go through, and does Section 9's normal-content-trivial obstruction still hold?
basis: The paper's final paragraph explicitly says 'The methods of this paper can also be applied to Grover's algorithm for multiple marked label search' but gives no computation. Our machinery (Parts C, D) generalises verbatim: replace j_0 with a subset J and re-check coset structure.
next_steps: Extend code/grover_hsp.py with an M-marked variant (oracle = -1 on any j in J, +1 else) for (N,M) in {(4,2),(8,2),(8,3),(16,4)}; re-verify P_success = sin^2((2k+1)\arcsin(\sqrt{M/N})); re-check that the setwise stabiliser has trivial largest normal subgroup for M < N-1; write up as a short note.

q: Since Part E shows Ind_{Stab_0}^{S_N}(1) = trivial + standard, does the 'standard representation of S_N' by itself encode j_0? Concretely: if we prepared the coset state |Stab_{j_0}> and projected onto the standard irrep block, does the resulting reduced density matrix depend on j_0? If yes, this hints at a 'restricted QHS' that could identify j_0 by measuring only within the standard block.
basis: In Part E we noted Ind_{Stab_0}^{S_N}(1) decomposes as trivial (dim 1) + standard (dim N-1). The trivial component is the same for every Stab_j (all coset states have the same overlap with the trivial character). But the standard component is j_0-labelled by its natural basis {|0>, ..., |N-1>}.
next_steps: For N=4, explicitly construct the standard-representation projector P_std of S_4 (dim 3) in the regular-rep basis; compute Tr_{Stab_j}[|Stab_j><Stab_j|] projected through P_std for j=0,1,2,3; check whether the 4 reduced states are pairwise orthogonal. If they are, that's essentially just Grover in disguise; if they overlap in a nontrivial way, it may open a new algorithmic angle.
